title: gpu-nsight-occupancy-analysis-2026-03-15
body:
TL;DR: Nsight runs on the 256-token generation workload show low achieved occupancy (12%-28%) and moderate SM utilization (~30%-50%) across A100 instances. Primary suspects: high register pressure per thread, many small kernels with short durations (high kernel launch overhead), and fragmented memory behavior (many small device loads).

Goal:
- Understand why per-GPU throughput isn't scaling linearly with batch size and why latency tails exist for 99th percentile.
- Produce actionable fixes/experiments (compile flags, kernel changes, scheduling tweaks) to increase occupancy and reduce per-request cost.

Environment / baseline:
- Model: transformer-decoder 7B variant (KV cache enabled, 2048 max seq provisioned, typical seq=256).
- HW: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100 40GB), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.x, NCCL 2.18, Nsight Systems 2024.5 (nsys).
- Runtime: Redwood serving-runtime v0.67 (kernel fusion opt enabled in graph path), using per-token generation loop with CUstream per inference.
- Workload: synthetic sampled prompt set, batch sizes tested {1,4,8,16}, token length=256 for steady-state throughput.
- Measurement toolchain: nsys profile + timeline exports (.qdrep -> .nvvp), nvtx ranges instrumented around major runtime regions (token loop, matmul, softmax, kv-copy).

What we ran (commands / profile snippets):
- nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=nsight-run-2026-03-14 \
  python -m serving_runtime.bench --model 7b --batch 8 --tokens 256 --warmup 20 --iters 200
- Collected kernel timeline and "gpu activity" summary from Nsight and exported metrics: SM utilization, achieved occupancy, active warps / SM, register utilization, shared mem usage, L2 throughput, DRAM throughput.

High level findings (summary):
- Achieved occupancy: 12%-28% across the heavy matmul kernels. The largest matmul kernels (gemm_simt / cutlass-based) reach ~25% occupancy. Several custom pointwise kernels are below 10% occupancy.
- SM utilization: 30%-50% for matmul heavy phases; peaks correlate with fused matmul+add+gelu kernels but are short (~0.4-1.2ms).
- Kernel duration distribution: large number (>40) of sub-ms kernels per token loop (many <200us). High kernel launch overhead and serialization visible on the timeline (gaps between kernels).
- Register pressure: compiler reports/NSight show ~80-120 registers used per thread for some fused kernels; this limits threads per block and therefore occupancy on A100 (theoretical max warps/SM not achieved).
- Memory: L2 hit rate moderate, DRAM throughput <50% of peak; we see bursts on device->host memcpy for logging path (should be off in perf runs).
- CUDA Graph usage: we attempted cuLaunchGraph for the steady-state token loop but the graph composition had many small kernels – graph reduces host overhead but didn't drastically increase occupancy because per-kernel resource limits remain.

Initial interpretation / root causes:
1) High register usage per thread -> limits resident warps -> low achieved occupancy. Likely due to aggressive kernel fusion (fused matmul + bias + gelu + layernorm) increasing register live values.
2) Too-fine-grained kernels -> many short-duration kernels produce high relative launch overhead and poor SM fill over time. Even with graphs, kernel-level resource limits remain the bottleneck.
3) Divergence / control flow in some pointwise kernels (attention masking, variable-length tokens) reduces warp efficiency.
4) Small IO/memory ops (kv-copy, small gathers) serialize and create gaps in GPU timeline; these could be batched or converted into larger contiguous ops.

Quantitative examples (from Nsight run for batch=8):
- Matmul_fused_1: duration 1.12ms, achieved occupancy 24%, SM util 48%, regs/thread ~96, shared mem ~0KB
- Pointwise_activate: duration 0.15ms, achieved occupancy 8%, SM util 12%, regs/thread ~60
- KV_copy_small: duration 0.04ms, many launches; contributes ~15% of total host->device sync gaps
- Overall token loop steady-state throughput: 320 tokens/sec per GPU (baseline target 540 tokens/sec)

Immediate recommendations (low-effort -> high-effort):
- Low effort:
  - Turn off some levels of fusion for hot kernels to reduce register pressure (experiment: disable fused gelu+bias for a single matmul path). Owner: Marco.
  - Rebuild with -maxrregcount=64 / 80 for the fused kernels to force spill (may hurt perf but increases occupancy; measure tradeoff). Owner: Daniel.
  - Increase native block sizes / adjust launch_bounds where possible for pointwise kernels. Owner: Priya.
- Medium effort:
  - Refactor very small kernels into a single combined kernel where memory access patterns align (e.g., batch kv-copy + reshape). This reduces launch overhead and increases per-kernel work. Owner: eng-serving-runtime squad alpha.
  - Add an experimental persistent-thread kernel for the token loop to amortize per-launch overhead for many small ops. Owner: Marco + Daniel.
- High effort:
  - Rework fused kernels to reduce register live range (split computation stages, reuse registers). Might require algorithmic changes or additional kernel launches but could increase occupancy. Owner: Performance team.
  - Investigate using CUTLASS/CUBLAS-backed GEMM kernels with tuned split-k to get better SM occupancy if our custom kernels are underperforming. Owner: Research/Applied-ML.

Micro-experiments to run (priority order):
1) Build baseline with -maxrregcount=80 for fused kernels and run batch {1,4,8,16} to measure tokens/sec and 99p latency. (quick, rollback safe).
2) Disable fusion for bias+gelu on top 2 hot matmuls and run nsys to compare regs/thread and occupancy.
3) Combine KV copy + permute into a single kernel for 2 layers and measure kernel counts and timeline gaps.
4) Implement a CUDA-graph version with aggregated small kernels per token step (group 5-10 operations) and measure host overhead reduction vs occupancy change.

Measurements to capture for each experiment (so we can compare):
- tokens/sec (steady-state), 50/95/99 latency, per-kernel achieved occupancy, SM utilization, regs/thread, warps/SM, L2 & DRAM throughput, kernel count per token loop.
- Also capture nsight timeline (qdrep) and an exported flame timeline png for quick triage.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is high reg usage coming from our codegen (XLA-like) or from compiler heuristics on fused kernels? Need to capture PTX/ASM for hot kernels and inspect register allocation.
- Could using float16 / tensor cores reduce register pressure and improve occupancy for matmuls? We need an experiment with mixed precision path toggled on.
- Are there CPU-side stalls or stream syncs causing artificial gaps? Timeline suggests gaps are mostly GPU-side but we'll double-check host->device synchronization points in code.

Risks and rollback plan:
- Forcing lower registers (-maxrregcount) can increase spills and L1/DRAM traffic; if tokens/sec drops, revert immediately. Keep perf CI for perf regression check.
- Disabling fusion might increase kernel count which can hurt latency due to more launches; test both tokens/sec and p99 latency.

Next steps & owners (concrete):
- Marco: run -maxrregcount=80 build and post results in the ticket JIRA-ENG-3321 by 2026-03-17.
- Daniel: instrument PTX dump for Matmul_fused_1 and attach to GH PR for discussion by 2026-03-18.
- Priya: prototype merged KV-copy+permute kernel for 2 layers and benchmark (due 2026-03-22).
- Performance team: schedule 2-hour pairing session to review Nsight timeline and walk through hot kernels (invite sent).

Notes / miscellaneous:
- We saw that CUDA graphs reduced host-side scheduling overhead by ~12% but didn’t meaningfully change SM occupancy – confirms resource limits rather than scheduling overhead are dominant for this workload.
- Logging path was accidentally enabled in one run (small host->device memcpys visible). Ensure perf runs use "--perf-mode" flag to disable debug logging.

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducibility:
- Use the nsight profile invocation above, attach --capture-range to the runtime's nvtx begin/end wrappers.
- Save qdrep and export timeline png and "gpu summary" csv.
- Collect gpustat and nvidia-smi topo output during runs.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add PTX/asm snippet to GH PR for Matmul_fused_1 (Daniel)
- [ ] Run -maxrregcount experiment and paste nsight csv into Jira (Marco)
- [ ] Prototype merged-kv kernel (Priya)
- [ ] Re-run with mixed precision enabled and compare occupancy (Marco + Research)

If you want, I can produce a condensed one-page summary for the exec update (perf improvement targets + risk matrix) or export the timeline screenshots into the linked nsight-reports folder.

End of doc.
